I shall now further explain the method for performing the preliminary practices (*pūrvasevā*).
One should place an image of the Principal Deity before a stūpa containing relics.
On the fifteenth day of the third month,
prepare the altar and make offerings according to one's means;
take agarwood and dip it in ghee, honey, and curd.
Perform *homa* by casting [offerings] into the fire day and night;
recite once for each casting into the hearth.
If the banners and flowers within the *maṇḍala* sway, [the rite is successful].
One should know that there is an efficacious result:
by making offerings to the Triple Gem at dawn for seven days,
one will obtain wealth, treasures, and official rank, all according to one's wishes.
Furthermore, regarding the acquisition of pearls, jade, the seven treasures,
and so forth; or if one wishes to cause fire to emerge from the sky,
one should gaze into the void and recite the mantra twenty-one times.
If one intends for fire to emerge from the sky, it shall do so.
Furthermore, if one desires rain, one should visualize the void and recite [the mantra] twenty-one times;
immediately, sweet rain will fall.
If one takes rainwater and offers it to the Buddha, all subsequent actions will be accomplished.
Furthermore, if one wishes for flowers to rain from the sky,
one should contemplate the void and recite [the mantra] twenty-one times.
Immediately, various flowers will rain down from the sky.
Furthermore, if one wishes to bring joy to either a man or a woman,
one should fashion pills from frankincense and recite [the mantra] twenty-one times.
If one recites his name once while casting it into fire, one will immediately attain joy.
Furthermore, if one consecrates sweet flag twenty-one times and holds it in the mouth,
one will prevail in all debates with others.
Furthermore, if Vināyakas should approach to harass or create obstacles,
they will all vanish the moment one recollects the mantra;
this is so provided one constantly recites it with uninterrupted and focused attention.
Those who obstruct [the practice], along with their kinsmen, shall all be destroyed of their own accord.
Furthermore, the rite begins on the first day of the dark fortnight;
facing the image, one should recite the mantra one thousand and eight times during each of the three periods of the day.
Perform homa by burning pills of an-xi (agallochum) incense;
by the end of the month, all that is sought shall be attained.
Furthermore, before the image, take lotus flowers and dip them in ghee, honey, and curd.
If one recites the mantra one thousand times and performs a homa by casting [an offering] into the fire, one will immediately obtain hidden treasures (*nidhi*).
Furthermore, for those seeking clothing,
one should enter a river flowing toward the sea and stand in the water up to the chest.
Take a flower with a stamen and recite the mantra one thousand and eight times;
by throwing it into the water once for each repetition, one will immediately obtain ten sets of garments.
Furthermore, another method is to soak *karṇikāra* flowers in ghee, honey, and curd.
Recite the homa mantra one thousand and eight times,
casting one offering into the fire with each recitation;
all sentient beings will thereby attain joy and submit in obedience.
Furthermore, there is another method:
before the image, take *sumana* flowers, dip them in ghee, honey, and curd, and perform *homa*.
For seven days, at three sessions each day, recite the mantra one thousand and eight times for each session.
If one casts [the substance] into the fire once for each person, all people will show him respect and he shall become the leader of the village.
Furthermore, if one wishes to subjugate a Śatru,
one should take human bone to fashion stakes and create the form of that person.
Alternatively, one may paint or mold [the effigy] and empower it one hundred and eight times;
by nailing it to the heart, one will immediately subjugate [the opponent].
Furthermore, if one wishes to destroy a *śatru* (enemy) who is a *māra*:
Take wood remaining from cremated corpses to fashion stakes;
grind red sandalwood incense and smear it upon the stakes;
take cloth from within a charnel forest and wrap the stakes with it.
Nail that *śatru* onto his head in the same form as before;
that *śatru* is indeed *mudrā*.
Now, the painting of the image of the noble Vajrakumāra is further explained.
His wrathful form is adorned with a tiger-skin skirt;
his right hand grasps a vajra,
and his left hand performs the gesture of offering a head.
Having performed the preliminary rites before the image at the stūpa containing the relics,
one should make offerings of incense and flowers to this image.
Before the image, construct a square incense burner.
To perform the rite of augmentation (*puṣṭi*), take agarwood the size of a thumb joint and anoint it with a mixture of ghee and oil. For seven days,
recite the mantra one hundred and eight times at each of the three daily sessions.
If one performs homa by casting [the substance] into the fire for seven full days,
one will attain the status of a vidyādhara with the *antardhāna* power,
such that the feet do not touch the ground and one travels as swiftly as the wind.
What one has heard shall never be forgotten.
Furthermore, for those who wish to accomplish the medicinal arts,
they should take the filaments of the *karṇikāra* flower, dragon-flower water, and white sandalwood incense.
These [ingredients] are to be finely pounded and thoroughly ground.

Furthermore, take elephant fat from an elephant twenty years of age whose forehead naturally has a fissure from which this distinct and extremely fragrant fat flows; take this fat and mix it with the aforementioned medicine to form pills.
When compounding the medicine, select a day under the lunar mansion of Ārdrā.
Have a young girl bathe and dress in fresh, clean garments,
then have her pound and sift the fragrant medicinal ingredients.
Prepare seven pills, each the size of a *wuzi* (nut) seed, and dry them in the shade.
Regarding the method for applying the medicinal pill: use the thumb and index finger to knead the pill until it softens, then smear it onto the area.
Furthermore, take bamboo membrane and attach it over the wax;
this is intended so that the prints of one's fingers do not appear on the medicinal paste above.
If there are fingerprints, the medicine will lack efficacy. As for the medicinal pills, they should be placed in a casket made of raw agarwood.
Facing the object, perform the purification and recitation at the three times of the day,
until a *khaṭa-khaṭa* sound arises within the vessel; then,
take one pellet and offer it to the deity.
Offer one pill with invocation;
offer one pill as a供养 (offering) to those who have previously attained accomplishment;
and divide one pill to share with your companions.
The remaining three pills are wrapped layer by layer with sheets of refined gold and silver.
By holding one in the mouth, one immediately attains the *āttādana* [power] to extinguish shadows and conceal one's form.
Furthermore, if one wishes to defeat an enemy:
Take flowers and place them upon the corpse.
Then, collect the remaining wood from the cremation and kindle a fire;
perform the homa for seven days.
During the dark phase of the moon, at midnight, or at noon, recite one hundred and eight times for each session.
Sit facing south before a triangular hearth and call upon the name of that general.
If one consecrates the aforementioned flowers once and casts them into the fire, that army will be immediately defeated.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause a pure-practicing brāhmaṇa to rejoice,
one should take *kulañjana* flowers.
Constantly reciting that name while performing *homā* within seven days,
and chanting the mantra while casting flowers into the fire, one will immediately attain his favor.
Furthermore, before a *śarīra* stūpa:
Take ox-gallstone and empower it one hundred and eight times.
Use it to mark the forehead;
all who see you wherever you travel will feel respect, affection, and joy.
Furthermore, take *kumāralatā* grass and *śāli* rice seedlings, dip them in clarified butter (*ghṛta*),
and perform one thousand and eight *homa* offerings,
casting each one into the fire as you complete each recitation.
One will immediately attain the total eradication of all calamities and the increase of one's lifespan.
Furthermore, regarding those who have already been subdued by this method,
if one wishes to alleviate their suffering:
If one performs *homa* with milk during the three periods of the day,
that suffering will be eliminated.
Furthermore, for those who wish to attain the power of hearing and retaining teachings without forgetfulness, such that they can recite ten thousand words daily:
Perform various offerings before the image of the Noble Krodhavajra.
Place clarified butter (*ghṛta*) in a silver vessel;
the method for taking the curd (*dadhi*) will be explained below.
From the time of recitation until the signs appear, one will attain the power of hearing and retaining [the teachings] without forgetting them.
Furthermore, for those who wish to prolong their lifespan,
they should drink milk and eat barley.
Recite the mantra one hundred thousand times before an image of Maheśvara;
take realgar and place it inside a vessel of refined copper.
Cover [the vessel] from above and below with seven leaves of the Bodhi tree as before,
and simultaneously offer gruel as an offering to the deities of the eight directions;
recite the mantra with a sincere heart.
Whether one has companions or is alone,
one should protect oneself by forming the armor-seal (kavaca-mudrā) and perform recitation until the three signs appear.
If one desires a lifespan of ten thousand years characterized by radiant marks,
or wishes to attain honor and respect,
one should fashion a wheel or a trident out of iron.
Place an image of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva before the śarīra stūpa;
perform extensive offerings and install it within the maṇḍala.
Place the right hand upon it and recite the mantra without interruption until a sound like "tsit tsit tsit" arises;
then you should know that accomplishment has been attained.
Holding a trident or a wheel in his hand,
all gods and humans will immediately submit to him and revere him as they would a Buddha.
Furthermore, take soil from both banks of a river, mold it into the shape of a thumb, and place it within the mandala.
Press the vajra against it while reciting the mantra;
when the vajra and the fingers come close to the body,
know that success has been achieved.
Thereafter, holding this finger with the hand,
if one wishes to summon the eight classes of beings— whether devas, nāgas, humans, women, or animals and beasts—
one should utter their respective names within the mantra syllables.
Arriving as swiftly as the wind,
they bring all that the practitioner commands and performs into complete submission.
Furthermore, there is a method for extending one's lifespan.
Construct a mandala with colored powders as an object of worship.
Place ox-gallstone (*gorocanā*) inside a vessel of refined copper.
Recite the mantra until light emanates from it; when held in the hand, one’s lifespan will be five thousand years.
Furthermore, there is another method: take seven portions of earthworm dung and clay, empower them with mantras, and smear them upon a circular altar.
Sit upon the altar and perform the recitation.
Furthermore, celestial sublime medicines will descend from the sky;
as soon as one grasps these medicines, one’s body becomes like that of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva.
Moreover, for those who wish to accomplish the Flower Rite:
Carve an open-blown lotus flower out of red sandalwood and perform recitations before a stūpa containing relics or an image.
When light appears, one will then transform into a vidyādhara.
It is most noble and venerable.
If one reaches the cave-dwellings where the vidyādhara sages reside,
all the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings will accord with one’s wishes.
Furthermore, there is a method for those bitten by venomous insects,
afflicted by malevolent spirits,
suffering from malaria, or poisoned by toxic drugs.
Consecrate water seven times with this mantra;
by sprinkling it upon the patient or having them drink it, they will be cured.
Furthermore, if one wishes to bind or subdue [an opponent], one should recite the *praśna* (question) syllables.
If one does not eat for one day and one night while performing recitations,
the rite will be accomplished.
Alternatively, a boy or a girl may be made to bathe and don new, clean garments.
Having smeared and purified a circular altar with mud, one should cause [the practitioner] to sit there.
By binding [the mantra], one comes to know all matters of the past and future.
Even if this person has committed the four grave offenses (pārājika) or the five crimes of immediate retribution (ānantarya), [this rite remains effective].
Regarding those who lack the portion of accomplishment in the present life:
by entering the maṇḍala and receiving empowerment,
they shall subsequently attain all accomplishments through recitation in this very life.
How much more so for one who maintains the full precepts and practices!

Furthermore, if one takes powdered ox-gall, empowers it one thousand and eight times with mantras, and applies it to the forehead, all people will see them with joy; even if in the midst of an army, blades and arrows shall not strike their bodies.
Furthermore, there is a method: at dawn, take a handful of water, empower it seven times with mantras, and drink it.
Then food and drink will arrive spontaneously without being sought.
Furthermore, by consecrating the corner of one’s *kāṣāya* twenty-one times, one will prevail in all debates and possess unhindered eloquence.
Another method: when passing through a territory infested with bandits...
If one recites with single-minded devotion, one will not be robbed or harmed.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one scatters ashes of *khadira* wood over the person performing the recitation, that recitation will become ineffective.
If one wishes to release [the binding], reciting the mantra once mentally will immediately effect its release.
Furthermore, when a woman is giving birth,
take one *liang* of clarified butter (*sarpis*), empower it twenty-one times with the mantra, and have her consume it.
Then one will give birth easily and not undergo various sufferings.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause an evil person to rejoice,
one should take wax and mold it into the shape of that person.
Place it upon your thigh and perform the empowerment one thousand and eight times;
all violent and wrathful persons will become respectful, compliant, and joyful.
Furthermore, before the image of the deity:
Offer one thousand and eight white flowers,
and all will immediately become reverent, compliant, and submissive.
Furthermore, the practitioner should drink milk or eat barley.
Take an earthworm and mold it into the form of the Naga King Vasuki;
sit upon that king and perform the recitation.
If it moves and shakes, you should know that the rite has been accomplished.
The Dragon King daily provided food for twelve people and also spoke of past and future events.
Furthermore, the Dharma practitioner lived on almsfood, beginning his begging from the first day of the month until the fourteenth day of the waxing moon.
One should perform extensive offerings and recitations before the image throughout the night;
when the image moves, one will immediately attain the *antarddhāna* (invisibility).
Among all accomplishments (*siddhi*), the *antarddhāna* is the most supreme.
If one mentally contemplates food and drink of a hundred flavors,
one will attain a lifespan of five thousand years.
Furthermore, according to another method, one enters the Ganges River and stands in the water up to the chest.
Recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
Thereafter, within the island of the Ganges,
empower sand stupas by means of mudrās.
Place the image of the deity on the bank of the river and perform homa with ghee,
honey, and curd mixed together;
all the nāgas will then descend and submit.
All matters for which one has made arrangements will be successfully accomplished.
Furthermore, there is a method: board a ship and enter the ocean, reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times.
The Dragon King of the Ocean immediately appears before him in person, and whatever he seeks is obtained; the dragon offers the practitioner a *maṇi* jewel.
Having received it, he becomes a vidyādhara and immediately soars into the void, becoming the most honored among all vidyādharas.
Furthermore, the ritual manual instructs that a goldsmith or copper-smith shall observe the eight precepts and fashion a "vase of the worthy" (*bhadraghaṭa*) from refined copper.

Within it, one should place a small portion of all types of seeds, such as grains and barley, as well as various medicinal herbs and small quantities of the seven precious substances, including gold and silver.
One should smear and cleanse the maṇḍala and perform offerings three times each day.
Place the flask within the altar.
Begin on the first day of the month of Ṛddhi.
Recite the mantra continuously until the fifteenth day.
Consecrate the flask;
light and flames will then appear from it.
Then, holding the argha water, one makes an offering to the noble assembly and expresses gratitude.
One immediately takes the vessel and places it in a clean location;
when any necessary items are required, one inserts the hand into the vessel.
All necessary wealth, treasures, vehicles, clothing, and playthings shall be obtained exactly as one desires;
the items produced from within the flask should first be offered to the primary deity.
The flask must be consecrated and protected;
otherwise, one fears that various māras may steal it and carry it away.
Furthermore, another method is to stand waist-deep in a river flowing into the ocean.
Recite the mantra one hundred thousand times.
Thereafter, fashion a stūpa out of either clay or sand,
and then extensively arrange offerings before the image.
Fashion a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*) out of crystal,
or alternatively, fashion one from clay and place it in the right palm;
sit in the full-lotus posture (*paryaṅka*), recite the mantra until light is emitted.
One will immediately become a wish-fulfilling jewel and attain the state of a vidyādhara.
Furthermore, there is another method: place an image before a reliquary stūpa on the fifteenth day of the month of Ṛddhi.
Before the image, perform extensive offerings according to the ritual rules and light lamps.
Holding a precious banner in the right hand with a white silk streamer tied to its top and hanging down,
recite the mantra until light is emitted.
One will immediately attain the status of a Vidyādhara with the Wish-Fulfilling Banner.
Furthermore, on the fifteenth day of the month of Ṛddhi,
one should perform extensive offerings before the image.
Take a case for the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra,
coat it with fragrant clay,
wrap it with flower garlands, and make offerings to it.
Place it in the left hand and sit in the full lotus posture.
Recite the mantra until light is emitted;
then one will attain unimpeded analytical knowledge regarding all Buddha-dharmas.
As a vidyādhara, he wanders through the six realms of existence to extensively benefit boundless sentient beings until they reach unsurpassed bodhi.
Furthermore, according to the ritual method, one should drink milk and eat barley.
At a solitary tree by the great seashore,
recite the mantra one thousand times at each of the three periods of the day;
then all the precious treasures within the great ocean will emerge, and you may take them as you please.
Furthermore, there is a method:
eat mung beans and recite the mantra one thousand and eight times on a mountain;
then you will see all the gold within the mountains and may take it as you please.
Furthermore, there is a method: empower ghee one thousand and eight times and give it to a woman who has no children; she will then conceive a son or daughter.
Furthermore, there is a method: take clarified butter (sarpis) and empower it one hundred and eight times.
Anointing one's body with [this substance], one enters fire without being burned and enters water without drowning.
If one recites the mantra while mindful of it, one will not be harmed by any poisons.
Furthermore, there is a method for performing the preliminary rites (*pūrvasevā*).
On the eighth and fourteenth days of the dark fortnight,
perform extensive offerings to the tutelary deity,
and immediately invite the saṃgha for a sequence of offerings.
Using realgar, draw a hundred-petaled lotus on the ground within the maṇḍala;
sit upon it and perform recitation until the earth cracks open and a lotus emerges.
Upon the petals of the lotus, sixteen vidyādhara sages soar through the sky in circumambulation.
If anyone should encounter such an accomplished one (siddha), [they will attain success].
They shall also attain the power to soar through the void;
this very lotus flower shall transform into a palace adorned with jewels.
At the end of their lifespan, which lasts for an intermediate kalpa, they shall be reborn in a pure and wondrous Buddha-land.
Furthermore, by consecrating water one thousand and eight times,
if it is used to irrigate withered trees, they will immediately produce flowers and fruit.
Moreover, if one recites mantras over a dried-up river, the water will become full once more.
Furthermore, if one is adrift and drowning in water, even if one knows how to swim,
should one become exhausted and lack the strength to recite the mantra, one will reach shallow water. Moreover,
one prays to bring joy to the great assembly of the Sangha.
Offer one thousand and eight flowers before the image, offering one flower for each recitation of the mantra;
by this method, one will obtain another rite: taking pills of *agaru* (sandalwood) incense, perform a homa sacrifice, and one will obtain one thousand *tolas* of gold.
Furthermore, there is another method: before the image, perform *homā* with *kunduruka* incense for seven nights.
Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times separately;
with each recitation, cast one offering into the fire, and you will immediately obtain hidden treasures (*nidhi*).
Furthermore, if one wishes to bring joy to an enemy, one should perform *homa* with white mustard seeds before an image for seven days;
at each of the three daily sessions, one should recite [the mantra] one thousand and eight times.
Reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times for each individual, cast them all into the fire;
immediately, all enemies will be subdued.
Furthermore, there is another method: empower oil one thousand and eight times.
Wounds from sword or arrow strikes will heal immediately upon being smeared with this.
Furthermore, take a clod of earth, empower it seven times, and cast it into the water;
all makaras, turtles, and tortoises therein will have their mouths clamped shut and will be unable to harm anyone.
Furthermore, by means of this mantra,
all diseases may be empowered so that they are entirely healed and cured.
Furthermore, for those suffering from pain throughout the body or from illnesses of chills and fever:
For one day, two days, or three days,
or for those who suffer from chronic illness,
empower sesame oil or sesame oil with one hundred and eight or twenty-one recitations.
If one uses it to smear the body,
[the affliction] will be cured immediately. Furthermore,
for *piśāca* malaria and the malaria caused by various *bhūta* spirits and demons, one should empower white thread with this mantra.
Tie a cord around [the patient] and they will immediately recover.
Furthermore, there is another method: take agarwood before an image of the Honored One and perform *homa* seven thousand times, using calf dung mixed with ghee, honey, and curd.
Then a yellow cow will arrive.
Furthermore, take the dung of its calf, mix it with ghee, honey, and curd, and perform homa twenty thousand times as before.
That cow will certainly come; one may take its milk and provide for a thousand people.
Furthermore, before the great general Pūrṇabhadra,
one should take *sumana* flowers and burn eight thousand of them daily for as long as six months;
one will then obtain one thousand strings of gold coins.
Furthermore, there is a method for making offerings to an image:
from the first day of the month until the fifteenth,
one should gradually increase the number of monks by one each day, beginning with an initial invitation of seven monks on the first day.
Once it is complete, the image will speak, saying:
"You have now achieved success;
henceforth, by reciting before this image, all that you seek shall be accomplished."
Furthermore, the ritual manual instructs that a young girl shall bathe and don fresh,
clean garments; she shall then join together threads of five colors and empower them one hundred and eight times.
If one ties it upon the right arm, diseases will be immediately eliminated and merit will increase.
Furthermore, at a river flowing toward the sea,
take black sesame seeds and grasp them with the tips of three fingers.
Recite the mantra once for each throw and each scoop into the water;
when eight thousand recitations are completed, one will obtain an abundance of grain and wheat.
Furthermore, every day take one hundred and eight fragrant flowers.
Recite the mantra once to empower it;
by making one offering to the Honored One, one shall obtain great merit.
Furthermore, there is another method: take a lily stem and kindle it as fire.
Take one thousand and eight pieces of achyranthes (chāṅpu).
Dip them in ghee and perform homa, casting one piece into the fire with each recitation of the mantra.
Take the ashes and apply them as a mark upon the forehead.
One will immediately attain the *āntardhāna* [power of invisibility].
If it is not accomplished on the first attempt, one must proceed to the second and third; then one will certainly achieve success.
Furthermore, beneath the Bodhi tree or under a *nyagrodha* tree, one may also make offerings to the image of the Noble One.
Take *agasti* grass, smear it with ghee, honey, and curd, and perform one thousand and eight *homa* offerings.
Immediately, elephants, donkeys, mules, oxen, water buffaloes, and the like will come of their own accord to follow and serve you as you command.
Furthermore, during the dark fortnight of the third month of spring, one should observe the eight precepts.
Before a stūpa containing relics, one should offer anointing with sandalwood, incense, and flowers,
and daily invite the saṃgha for a meal in succession.
Take four pieces from the bottom of a clay jar that are not blackened;
fill them with water,
and place small portions of various incenses and various medicinal herbs inside the jars.
Recite the mantra over each vessel to consecrate it.
On the morning of the eighth day of the dark fortnight, before the crowing of the cock,
have the men and women bathe.
Before the image of the *iṣṭadevatā*, take fire from a cremation ground used for burning corpses and charred wood;
take *yava* flowers and perform *homa*.
Recite the mantra one hundred thousand times, casting one flower into the fire at the end of each cycle.
One will immediately obtain food and drink in inexhaustible abundance,
which one should extensively bestow as gifts and offerings.
Furthermore, regarding the method for those who are imprisoned or bound in shackles:
Upon reciting the mantra, one immediately attains liberation.
Furthermore, during the month of Ṛddhi, one should consume milk and eat barley before an image of the deity.
If one recites without interruption from the thirteenth to the fifteenth day,
the Noble One will appear;
the lamp flame will blaze intensely and the earth will tremble.
The image moves and emits a voice, saying to the practitioner:
"You have now achieved success;
henceforth, whatever you seek through recitation before this image shall all be obtained."
Furthermore, according to another method, if one recites the mantra one hundred thousand times before a stūpa containing relics,
all grave sins committed that would otherwise lead to rebirth in the evil realms shall be entirely extinguished.
Furthermore, there is another method: every day before the cock has crowed, take seven grains of black pepper and empower them twenty-one times;
by swallowing them oneself, one will immediately attain the power of hearing and retaining all that is heard.
Recite this one hundred and fifty times daily, casting each repetition separately into the fire;
whatever you seek—honorable office, wealth, intelligence, or increased longevity—you shall obtain it all.
Furthermore, there is another method: [perform this] on both banks of a river.
A person from afar asked about the place where the sound of the pestle for pounding silk was heard.
[The master] took earth and fashioned a square altar measuring seven cubits.
Upon the altar, he drew a thousand-petaled lotus flower.

Upon the lotus, using the measurement of one *vitasti* of a Tathāgata— which is equivalent to one *hasta* for an ordinary person— one should take five kinds of metal— gold, silver, copper, iron, and tin—
and melt them together into a single disc, which is then placed upon the flower.
Offer various kinds of flowers around the four sides of the maṇḍala.
Light seven butter lamps.
Place four vases filled with scented water at the four cardinal directions.
Place a small amount of the seven precious gems inside the flask and set a *kūṭaja* fruit upon it.
One should burn *kunduruka*, *agaru*, *śrīveṣṭaka*, and *guggulu* incense.
One should provide divine food for the four directions:
in the east, offer rice with curd;
in the south, offer rice mixed with water.
In the west, offer cooked rice with sugar;
in the north, offer milk-rice gruel.
These are placed before this mandala.
Kindle a fire with palāśa wood and take one thousand pieces of uśīra grass;
perform the homa by anointing them with clarified butter.
First, perform the empowerment seven times.
Then, cast one stalk of *gokṣura* into the fire for each recitation until the wheel is filled and emits light.
Holding this wheel, one immediately attains the power to soar through the void.
All the vidyādhara sages will submit to one’s will and serve with reverence as if to a Buddha.
Furthermore, on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon during a lunar eclipse, [one should perform the rite].
The practitioner receives the eight precepts and fasts for one day and one night before a stupa containing relics.
He then takes *gomaya* (cow dung) that has not yet fallen to the ground.
Anoint a circular mandala approximately the size of a hide of ox leather.
Take a yellow dairy cow whose calf is of the same color as its mother,
and have a young girl milk the curds to produce clarified butter (*ghṛta*).
Take seven *liang* of clarified butter and place it in a vessel of gold or silver.
Holding the butter with the left hand,
stir it with the ring finger of the right hand.
Recite the mantra to empower it;
if one drinks it while it is warm, one will attain the power of hearing and retaining [the teachings] without forgetting, such that one can recite ten thousand words daily.
After a single recitation, one shall never forget them for the rest of one's life.
If the sign of smoke appears, all who see it will love, revere, and honor [the practitioner].

If the sign of light appears, one should offer *āntardāna* and clarified butter as an offering; furthermore, during a solar eclipse, one should follow the previously mentioned ritual. Moreover, if an epidemic is spreading through a city or village...
At midnight, smear a small mandala and offer white food.
Take wood from milky trees to kindle a fire,
and perform one thousand and eight oblations of clarified butter (*ghṛta*) into the fire.
Reciting the name of the king individually for each [offering], one casts ghee into the fire; thus diseases will be removed from the realm.
Furthermore, if one wishes to subjugate yakṣas:
Take ten-finger-length pieces from a nyagrodha tree, dip them in ghee, honey, and curd, and perform one thousand and eight *homa* offerings; the spirit will be subdued.
Furthermore, to subdue epileptic spirits that suck the vital essence of humans:
If one performs a homa with black sheep’s wool one thousand and eight times,
that ghost will submit and the patient will be cured.
Furthermore, if one wishes to subjugate Maheśvara:
Take frankincense and fashion one thousand and eight pills.
Anoint them with clarified butter and perform one thousand and eight *homa* offerings.
[This shall subdue] all the messengers belonging to Maheśvara.
All shall be subdued and every task accomplished.
Furthermore, there is a rite: take one *liang* of realgar and set its price according to whatever is requested.
Use firewood from the *palāśa* tree— also called *madhūka*— to kindle a fire.
Once the realgar has been burned until it takes on the color of fire,
one should collect it and place it in a vessel of refined copper.
Pour ghee over the top of the realgar.
As for the ghee, take that from a mother and calf of the same color;
have a young girl milk the cow, and let the curds ferment to extract the ghee.
Take curd and honey-curd,
placing each separately in its own vessel to offer to the Honored One;
then collect the realgar.
Place it inside a vessel made of refined copper.
During a lunar eclipse,
observe a three-day fast from the thirteenth to the fifteenth day.
Facing north before a śarīra stūpa,
take seven bodhi leaves;
arrange four beneath as a base and three above as a cover.
Recite the mantra without interruption.
If the sign of "warmth" appears, apply it to your forehead;
all who see you will be filled with joy. If the sign of "smoke" appears...
Then, the *ānattadana* (invincibility) is accomplished;
if the sign of light appears,
one will fly up into the void.
In this manner, by relying on the aforementioned method,
one will achieve success in the rites for realgar, ox-gallstone, and añjana; however,
the rite for ox-gallstone alone differs slightly from this.
Regarding the rite for cow bezoar: on the fifteenth day of the month,
wrap the cow bezoar in a lotus leaf and place it within both hands with palms joined.
Recite the mantra continuously with empowerment until the three signs appear;
the resulting karmic fruit will be as previously described.
Furthermore, there is another method: fashion a lotus flower from the five precious metals.
Take saffron, ox-gall, and camphor, grind them into a powder, and mix with rainwater to form seven pills.
If one places the image before a stūpa containing relics and performs recitation,
pressing it with the right hand until light is emitted,
one will then fly up into the void as a vidyādhara with a lifespan of ten thousand years.
If one consecrates a crown, armlets, or a waistband with mantras, all will achieve accomplishment as previously described;
even if one has broken the precepts or corrupted one's conduct, whatever one undertakes shall still be accomplished.
How much more so for one who possesses the precepts and practices accordingly!
Furthermore, taking the dung of a calf and performing *homa* for seven days,
recite the mantra one thousand and eight times at one specific time each night.
If one takes a small amount of *gomaya* (cow dung) and throws it into the fire once, one will obtain one hundred head of cattle.
Furthermore, there is another method:
standing waist-deep in a river, take a lotus flower, smear it with sandalwood paste until it is like mud, and recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times.
Cast each one individually into the water;
the hidden treasure obtained will accumulate like lotus flowers.
Furthermore, there is another method: take one thousand and eight pieces of auspicious wood.
Perform a ghee-homa for three days, reciting one thousand and eight times at each of the three daily sessions, and you will obtain abundant wealth and treasures.
Furthermore, there is another method: take black sesame seeds and rice blossoms and mix them together.
Perform homa before the image for three days;
at each of the three sessions per day, recite one thousand and eight times,
casting one oblation into the fire with each recitation.
One will immediately obtain inexhaustible food and drink within one's home.
Furthermore, if one wishes to subjugate all dragon kings,
one should perform homa with various kinds of flowers for three days.
If one recites it one thousand and eight times for each of the three periods of the day,
all nāgas will be subdued.
Furthermore, if one wishes to subdue yakṣas:
Facing the image, take guggulu resin pills and perform homa for seven days, three times each day,
one thousand and eight times per session.
One will immediately achieve the subjugation of all yakṣas.
Furthermore, regarding the method for summoning a yakṣiṇī:
take aśoka wood and perform a homa according to the previously described yakṣa-homa rite.
Immediately, a yakṣiṇī will come to serve him with reverence,
providing all necessary clothing, food, drink,
and various treasures according to his wishes.
Furthermore, there is another method: before the fundamental image,
take sandalwood and dip it in ghee,
performing homa twenty-one times each day at three sessions.
If one recites it separately one thousand and eight times,
all the devas will immediately rejoice and provide protection;
calamities and misfortunes will be extinguished, and merit and virtue will increase.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one is imprisoned,
by bathing at night and donning fresh, clean garments,
one shall attain liberation by reciting the mantra one thousand and eight times.
Furthermore, if one is met with anger by another who wishes to cause harm, one should perform *homa* with sesame seeds one thousand and eight times; that person will then become joyful.
Another method is to recite the mantra over sweet flag (*achyranthes aspera*) one thousand and eight times while consecrating it.
Tie it upon one's arm;
when speaking to others, whatever one requests shall be obtained according to one's wishes.
Furthermore, one should constantly recite it.
One will achieve victory over all enemies and shall not be oppressed by them.
Furthermore, there is a method: take a banner or flag and recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times.
Then, offer incense, flowers, and seven bowls of curd to the banner or flag as an offering.
Having offered arghya water,
he immediately took this banner and led his army forward;
upon seeing the banner, the enemy host broke apart of its own accord.
Furthermore, if a city or town is being plundered,
one should take yellow flowers before the image and perform *homa* for seven days,
reciting the mantra one thousand and eight times each day before the image.
Recite the mantra once and cast it once into the fire.
Any cities or towns previously seized by others will all be recovered.
Furthermore, there is a method for performing the preliminary rites (*pūrvasevā*).
Perform homa with white mustard seeds for seven days and seven nights;
within one month, treasures will rain down upon that dwelling.
Furthermore, there is another method: make offerings of incense and flowers before the image.
Drink milk and eat barley;
take lotus stalks, smear them with ghee, and perform one thousand and eight *homa* offerings. One will obtain one thousand *tolas* of gold.
Furthermore, there is a method: take one hundred thousand stalks of red lotus and perform one hundred thousand homa offerings;
whatever one desires will be entirely attained.
Furthermore, there is a method: take ten thousand white lotus flowers, dip them in ghee, and perform ten thousand homa offerings.
One will immediately attain a promotion to a high-ranking official position.
Furthermore, take white sandalwood and smear it with oil;
perform one hundred thousand *homa* offerings,
and you will immediately obtain one thousand gold coins.
Furthermore, there is a method: take agallochum (*agaru*) and perform *homa* one hundred thousand times.
At each repetition, cast one portion into the fire while reciting ten thousand words daily.
One will never forget any of the sūtras previously heard by ear, even for the rest of one's life.
Furthermore, there is another method: take a yellow dairy cow whose calf is of the same color;
milk her to produce curds, and churn them into butter.
Place this in a golden vessel and recite the mantra over it one hundred thousand times while performing consecration.
He immediately ate it.
He attained the power of hearing and retaining [the teachings] without forgetting, reciting ten thousand words daily.
Furthermore, there is a method: take *dhātrī* fruits, smear them with fragrant oil, and perform one hundred thousand *homa* offerings.
All those who are imprisoned or bound shall attain liberation.
Furthermore, if one recites the mantra mentally upon seeing an enemy,
that person will give rise to a mind of loving-kindness and will be unable to cause harm.
Furthermore, for all illnesses,
one should recite the mantra to empower a willow branch;
by brushing [the patient] with it, they will immediately be cured.
Furthermore, there is a method: take thread of five colors and tie them into a cord; empower it seven times and fasten it to the arm.
All malevolent spirits and demons will then be driven far away.
Furthermore, there is a method: empower clean ashes seven times and scatter them around the altar;
this immediately constitutes a boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*).
Another method concerns women who do not conceive children.
After menstruation, take cow’s milk that is the same color as the mother and her child;
empower it one hundred and eight times and have the woman prostrate before the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas before drinking it.
Furthermore, boil milk porridge mixed with ghee and empower it one hundred and eight times;
by administering it, a son endowed with merit and auspicious marks will be born.
Another method is to perform the preliminary rites (*pūrvasevā*).
Make offerings of incense and flowers before the image.
Take aloeswood the size of a thumb joint,
dip it in ghee and oil, and perform homa for seven days.
Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times during each of the three periods of the day.
For each recitation, cast [a portion] once into the fire.
One will then attain the siddhi of the vidyādhara-anuttana.
The feet leave the ground as one walks swiftly, and one attains the power of hearing and retaining [teachings] without forgetting.
From the *Āryakāṇimāraktayamāri-tantrarāja-nāma-sādhanopāyikā*, Middle Fascicle:
The Ritual for the Accomplishment of the Bodhisattva Āryakāṇimāraktayamāri-vajrakumāra.
Ritual Manual, Scroll Lower.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Tang Dynasty.
I shall now explain the method for binding and striking with mudrās.
First, smear a circular mandala measuring one cubit with *gomaya* (cow dung).
Take a boy or girl aged seven or eight, dressed in new, clean garments;
first cause them to purify themselves for three days and have them stand within the mandala.
Burn benzoin incense;
first empower the incense seven times and then burn it.
Furthermore, take flowers and empower them seven times.
Place the youth in the center and have him cover his face.
Then, the practitioner forms the mudrā and recites the mantra.
The practitioner faces east, while the youth faces west.
For this mudrā, form fists by interlacing the two hands with the palms facing inward;
hook the two little fingers together and extend the two thumbs upward, side by side.
Forming it like the shape of a hook and chain, place it upon the forehead;
firmly seize that young boy and speak these words.
He thrusts the two index fingers outward;
the boy then retreats and walks backward.
He beckons the two index fingers toward his body.
The youth immediately comes forward;
this constitutes the hook-summoning.
One should brandish the mudrā to the left and right over the youth.
Then, following the left and right movements of the mudrā, one strikes and raises the mudrā upward; the youth will immediately stand up.
One may then inquire of him regarding matters of good or ill fortune throughout the three periods of time.
Each and every one shall truly accomplish their tasks with speed.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi spoke in verse:
"This Vajra Youth is born from my samādhi."
Accomplishing all activities, I am Vajrapāṇi, the wrathful king of great power;
I subdue those who are difficult to tame and can utterly extinguish the sins of the most violent yakṣas.
And the hosts of rākṣasas who afflict and harm practitioners—
may they be swiftly extinguished. May Brahmā, Śakra, Varuṇa,
and the various celestial kings, as well as other beings of majestic power [protect them].
One should cause [them] to perish in an instant;
the practitioner should enter the samādhi of the Wrathful King.
Possessing a majesty like a vajra, he can subdue those who are difficult to tame, causing them all to submit and obey.
Furthermore, by taking lotus flowers or fragrant flowers and performing homa,
one shall obtain whatever is sought.
Moreover, by forming the mudrā and reciting the mantra of the syllable HŪṂ, [the same result is achieved].
It can cause mountains and peaks to crumble and collapse;
it can also dry up the waters of rivers;
and it can shatter the bolts and bars of the asuras.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva addressed the great assembly, saying:
"This King of Wrath possesses immeasurable majesty and great supernormal powers;
he is well able to subdue those who are difficult to subdue."
He demonstrates various skillful means.
From this samādhi, this bodhisattva is born;
as soon as he brings it to mind, all malevolent spirits and ghosts flee in every direction.
All sentient beings with malicious minds shall be destroyed,
and all calamities shall be entirely eliminated.
If there be anyone who receives and maintains this mantra, [these benefits shall accrue].
One naturally comes to possess the samaya vows;
if one seeks siddhi, it will be swiftly attained and cannot be thwarted.
One shall not fall into the evil realms, but will quickly realize the bodhisattva stages and attain unsurpassed enlightenment.
If one recites it even once,
all calamities and misfortunes will be eliminated, and one will be able to restrain tigers, wolves, lions, malevolent nāgas, and the like.
By consecrating a clod of earth and throwing it upon their bodies, they will be unable to cause harm.
If one's natal constellation (*janmanakṣatra*) is threatened by the sun, moon, or the five planets,
one will not encounter calamities provided one can constantly recite [this mantra].
If used to eliminate the misfortunes of others, it is likewise effective.
If one performs homa with white mustard seeds mixed with milk while reciting the name of the person, their misfortunes will be pacified.
This also applies if they have been seized by a rākṣasa or a ghost.
If one is oppressed or harmed by enemies,
by reciting the mantra one will immediately attain liberation, and the enemies will turn toward one with a heart of loving-kindness.
Furthermore, if there is litigation or dispute, [the same shall apply].
Perform a homa sacrifice with *sumana* flowers for seven nights;
recite one hundred and eight times each night, casting one flower into the fire at each repetition, and disputes will be extinguished.
If one practices thus:
One should enter this maṇḍala and receive empowerment.
One must demarcate the ground and draw the lines;
the ācārya should purify that site.
Construct the altar using threads of five colors;
the altar shall be eight cubits, twelve cubits, or sixteen cubits in size,
according to the ritual procedures previously explained.
It has four gates on the four sides.
In the center, one should paint the Great Wrathful King Vajra-sūru-sūru,
holding a vajra in his hand.
To the right of Vajrapāṇi,
depict the Vidyā Vajrāṅkuśī from the Vajra family;
to her right, depict the Mahāpāṇḍaravāsini Vidyā.
On the southern side, one should depict the Great Terrifying Eye of the Krodhavajra who Strides (Kramavikrāmin) and others.
On the right side, one should depict the ten Hard-to-Behold Wrathful Vajras (Durdṛśa-krodhavajras), namely:
the Hard-to-Behold Wrathful Vajra and the Water-Wrathful Vajra.
The wrathful vajra Aparājita; the wrathful vajra Devatāḍaka;
the wrathful vajra Sumeru; and the wrathful vajra Ratnaśikhara.
The Wrathful Vajra Trilokavijaya, the Blazing Radiance of the Wrathful Vajra;
and on the northern side, the ten vajras such as the blue staff, namely:
the Blue Staff Vajra and the Muṣṭika Vajra.
Kāpilavajra, Mahāhāsavajra, Vikramavajra, Utkrāntikramavajra, and Maheśvarakramavajra.
First is the Vajra of the Thunderbolt;
then the Vajra of the Great Club for Subduing;
and in the western direction, one should paint the eight great Vajras, such as Aparājita and the others.
That which is called the Invincible Vajra Wrathful Vajra,
the Unbearable Vajra Terrifying Vajra,
the Utterly Wrathful Vajra, and the Vajra of the Three Times.
Having accomplished the Great Wrathful Vajra,
if one desires to gain victory over hostile enemies or wicked persons,
[one should perform this] at each of the four gates within the maṇḍala.
On the right side, paint the Bodhisattva Vajrabhairava;
on the left side, paint Cundāvajra.
At the four outer gates, [paint the same].
On the right, paint the wrathful Vajra-āśani;
on the left, paint the wrathful Vajra-śṛṅkhala.
In front of these two wrathful Vajras, [place...]
One should depict the devas, asuras, nāgas, and māras,
assuming terrifying postures of submission.
On the outer boundary path of the maṇḍala, one should draw the various hosts of devas.
Place perfumed ointments, seasonal flowers, food offerings,
and lamps around the four sides of the maṇḍala to make offerings to all the bodhisattvas and Vajra-vidyārājas;
invite each of these holy ones with their respective root mantras.
Having performed the invitation, present the offering of arghya.
Form the mudrās and recite the mantras for inviting the various noble beings,
each presenting their respective samaya-mudrā.
Thereafter, the disciple is led into the maṇḍala to cast a flower;
according to the place where the flower lands upon a deity,
the master then bestows the mantra of that respective tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā).
One should immediately undergo consecration;
within this great maṇḍala of the Great Wrathful One,
one's sought-after supreme aspirations and the subduing of enemy forces will be fully realized.
By entering this maṇḍala, all pestilential diseases,
malevolent spirits, and all obstacles shall be completely extinguished;
furthermore, within this altar, one can also accomplish all medicinal substances.
With the *anta-dāna* [mantra],
one enters the palace of the asuras and achieves complete success.
At that time, the Vajra Secret Lord...
Beholding all sentient beings of the future,
for their benefit and happiness,
he briefly explains the accomplishment of all maṇḍalas.
With few material riches and a short period of time,
the reciter need only abide purely in the precepts,
while being accompanied by pure practice.
Alternatively, one may begin the practice of constructing the maṇḍala on the first day, second day, fifth day, eighth day,
or fourteenth day of the waxing moon, or on the fifteenth day of the full moon;
one should commence on such days as these.
Whether within the city or outside the city,
in a monastery or in a village, town, or settlement—
specifically in a tranquil place to the northeast where flowers and fruits abound, where there are groves of trees, fragrant blossoms, and soft grasses.
In the month of Ṛddhi (Ṛddhimāsa), one establishes the maṇḍala as described in the Guhya-sūtra;
having completed the purification of the site, the cleansing of the ground, and the demarcation of the sections.
One should draw the maṇḍala of the noble Vajrakumāra.
This altar is capable of accomplishing all great matters and possesses majestic power.
If one practices while possessing all the vows and relying upon the Susiddhi-tantra-rāja, [the goal will be attained].
Furthermore, regarding the swift accomplishment based on the most excellent sūtras,
as for all those malevolent spirits who create obstacles,
as well as the various forms of the nine grahas, whether holy or ordinary;
As soon as his name is uttered, they scatter and flee in all directions.
If one beholds this maṇḍala and receives initiation,
one then obtains the samaya vows.
Thereafter, one should receive from the master the mantras, mudrās,
and ritual procedures, thereby attaining accomplishment according to the methods previously explained in the Vajrarāja Sūtra.
If there are those who are diligent and courageous, they will achieve it without doubt.
At that time, Vajraguhyapati addressed the assembly of devas, saying:
"In the age of the final dharma, those who practice this teaching..."
There may be those who are indolent and fail to maintain the vows of mantra-discipline,
or there may be malevolent nāgas, thunderbolts,
and various māras who manifest in diverse bodily forms to disturb and harass the practitioner engaged in recitation.
As well as the various pūtana spirits, the spirits that suck the vital essence of humans,
and those among the deva realms who have transgressed as rākṣasas,
along with the hosts of the Devamātṛs and others.
Or they may be on Mount Sumeru or upon various jewel mountains in places of adornment;
by the sides of mountain rivers, peaks, and cliffs, in caves, forests, and wilds;
or amidst great rivers, marshes, large trees, great streams, and the great ocean.
Under trees with pleasing flowers and fruits by misty marshes and ponds;
in mountain regions where clouds arise and rain falls;
and at all spirits of old gardens and ancient shrines.
They mostly dwell in the aforementioned places,
delighting in creating obstacles and seeking out the faults of others;
if one does not rely on the prescribed methods, those Māras will immediately find an opportunity.
For the sake of such various sentient beings as these,
I have taught this Dharma so that those who maintain and recite it shall not be taken advantage of by any māras.
I, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
out of compassion for sentient beings, manifest in the form of a wrathful king of mantras;
by the power of this mantra, [this is accomplished].
All yakṣas, rākṣasas, and hosts of devas who behold me are struck with great terror.
Among all those seeking the methods for attaining accomplishments, and among all the mantras and wrathful deities, I am the supreme king.
Out of compassion for those sentient beings who are difficult to tame and who create obstacles,
he spoke this mantra in order to subdue them,
manifesting this form within samādhi.
It flows forth from his forehead;
therefore, this mantra is peerless, of great majesty, a great wrathful one, greatly terrifying, and of great renown,
for the sake of protecting the king and the True Dharma.
I, the Lord of Secrets, shall teach the Vajrakumāra rite.
Within this teaching, one should perform rites for pacification, enrichment, and subjugation.
Should there be those who harbor wrong views toward the Buddha’s teachings or, with hearts poisoned by hatred, seek to extinguish the True Dharma;
One should generate a fierce mind and perform the rite of subjugation (*abhicāra*).

If one wishes to alleviate the various sufferings and afflictions that the subjugated person undergoes, one should perform *homa* using wood from milky trees; thus, pacification (*śānti*) will be attained.
I shall now further explain the mudrā that accomplishes all matters when seeking siddhi.
The mantra for consecrating the object to be accomplished is as follows:
Oṃ kaṇi-kuruḍa sarvasattvabodhikara rakṣa rakṣa sarvanaravinye svāhā. This is the mudrā for bathing.
Following the previous method for the single-pronged mallet mudrā,
place both thumbs side by side within the palms;
when the wrists are joined together, it is completed.
The mantra is:
Oṃ kaṇi-kurara-ñca svāhā. The mantra for sweeping the ground of the maṇḍala is:
*Kaṇimāraya hūṃ*. When seeking accomplishment, for those who are difficult to subdue,
follow the previous root mudrā,
but cross the thumbs within the palms.
The mantra is:
Oṃ kaṇiśūṣaya sarvān uṣṇīṣān bandhaya bandhaya hūṃ phaṭ. This is the Great Vajra Heart Seal.
Following the previous method for the single-pronged vajra mudrā,
press the two thumbs together within the palms;
this is the Great Vajra Mind-At-Will Mudrā.
Following the previous heart-seal, join the two thumbs together and extend them upright;
this is also called the Lotus-Vajra Seal,
or the Most Victorious Heart-Seal.
Following the previous *jyeṣṭhamudrā*,
bend the two little fingers so that their tips touch one another.
This [is used] when there are various obstacles, difficulties, or inauspicious events within the home.
By forming this mudrā and reciting [the mantra], all [obstacles] will be extinguished.
This is the Supreme Mind-Compliant Mudrā (Cittānugata-mudrā).
It follows the previous Supreme Mudrā (Parama-mudrā).
Extend the two middle fingers.
This mudrā can accomplish all tasks;
even when entering the palace of the asuras, one uses this mudrā, which possesses great power.
Next, the Great Hook Seal (*mahā-aṅkuśa-mudrā*) is described:
with the two hands joined with the fingers interlaced inwardly,
bend the two index fingers into the shape of hooks.
This seal can summon all classes of sentient beings within the three realms.
If one summons an asura woman, she will arrive within seven days.
Furthermore, the Gaṇakī mudrā is described as follows:
it is like the single-pronged mudrā mentioned previously;
extend both little fingers and join the tips of both index fingers together.
Interlace the remaining six fingers within and count them open with the two thumbs;
this not only releases Naṭakī.
It can also eliminate all malevolent spirits dwelling upon the earth;
for this, one employs the root mantra.
Furthermore, it describes the mudrā for subduing all nāgas.
Following the previous method for the single-pronged mace mudrā,
bend the thumbs into the palms so that their nails face each other directly.
Visualize that dragon within the joint of the thumb;
this mudrā can subdue all dragons,
bringing about both rain and its cessation.
When all the nāgas see this seal,
they will flee far away in dispersal;
it can also eliminate the bites of all venomous insects.
By the power of this seal, one shall not be harmed by any poisons;
should one have already been injured, they will immediately recover.
Furthermore, it is said to be the seal for expelling all beings who are difficult to subdue.
Interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward;
join the two thumbs at their fourth joints.
This mudrā possesses great power.
All the powerful devas and malevolent spirits who do not comply with the teachings can be driven away by means of the root mantra.
Furthermore, there is a method using aragvadha.
Write the person’s name with vermilion on the palm;
heat the palm with fire while reciting the mantra, inserting the person’s name into the words of the mantra. In an instant, they will arrive.
Furthermore, recite the root mantra one hundred thousand times.
Thereafter, take *agaru* (sandalwood) incense and fashion one hundred thousand pellets for *homa*.
[This shall subdue] all yakṣiṇīs and vikecānīs.
One is able to summon them all and employ them in various ways.
Furthermore, if there is a calamity or a place of terror,
one should recite the mantra eight thousand times.
Then one will obtain the extinction of calamities and be freed from fear.
Furthermore, before an image of the Wrathful King,
one should perform homa with rice cooked in non-glutinous rice, mixed with clarified butter.
Then one will obtain inexhaustible food and drink within the household.
Furthermore, by taking the ashes of a *homa* offering and applying them to the crown of the head,
one will not be harmed by swords or clubs when entering an army formation.
One shall achieve victory over enemies.
Furthermore, if there is an epidemic in a city, town, or village,
one may enter the water and recite the mantra for seven nights, performing one thousand and eight recitations each night.
All epidemics will be completely eliminated.
Furthermore, if one seeks wealth and treasures,
one should wear new, clean clothes and stand before the image.
Smear a small altar with fragrant mud,
burn安息香 (an-shi-xiang, *agaru* or *sthalapadminī*) incense, and recite the mantra ten thousand times;
then one will obtain all that is wished for.
Furthermore, according to another method, one should focus the mind exclusively before the image and recite the mantra three hundred thousand times;
then one will see the Sage, and all that is sought shall be attained.
Furthermore, if there is prolonged torrential rain,
empower white mustard seeds one hundred and eight times; then,
cast them individually upward, scattering them into the void.
Then the rain will cease.
Furthermore, there is another method: take the corpse of a man that has not yet decomposed and go to a cemetery or a crossroads.
First, administer medicine to induce purging and rinse with water;
once the foul substances within the abdomen have been expelled,
further cleanse the body with fragrant decoctions until it is pure.
He anointed his entire body with fragrant unguents,
wrapped his loins in fine silk,
and adorned himself with flower garlands.
Take khadira wood and recite the mantra seven times over it; then,
empower a wooden stake made of khadira and drive it into the side of the head,
binding the hair to the top of the stake.
The practitioner sits upon the heart of the corpse,
facing east,
giving rise to a mind of loving-kindness, with vigor and intrepidity.
In the four directions, one should station four practitioners of mantra who hold swords.
The reciter, holding a small iron ladle,
shall scoop up iron filings and pour them into the mouth of the corpse.
Without interrupting the recitation, the corpse’s tongue will emerge;
cut off the tongue with a sharp blade,
and it will transform into a sword held in the right hand.
His complexion is like that of a blue lotus;
together with his retinue, he soars through the void,
becoming a Vidyārāja with a lifespan of one great kalpa.
One shall be born in the palace of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
Furthermore, there is a method for conducting a transaction with spirits in a śmaśāna (cremation ground),
selling a mahāmāṣa to the spirits.
When taking longevity elixirs, *tadana* medicines, precious swords, hidden treasures, gold, silver, or the seven jewels,
one should employ this mantra during the performance of the rite to protect oneself and one's companions.
All shall attain unimpededness and will not be deluded by the illusions of demons; whatever they seek shall be accomplished.
Furthermore, if one wishes to defeat an enemy force, the generals and all subordinates below them must each empower their bodies seven times with this mantra for protection.
The enemy will be defeated immediately.
Alternatively, by consecrating water one thousand and eight times with a mantra and sprinkling it over the troops, they will not be harmed.
One will attain liberation from them, and the enemies will retreat and disperse.
Furthermore, there is another method: take four ceramic jars whose bottoms are not black, fill them to the brim with river water, and...
Then, having applied a small amount of various fragrances and medicinal herbs,
empower them one hundred and eight times before the image and pour them over the crown of the head.
If that person has practiced recitation for a long time and exerted great effort yet still receives no manifest signs of efficacy,
being afflicted by various māras and troubled by inauspicious ghosts and spirits,
it is because they have performed this rite of consecration and ritual bathing.
All malevolent spirits and demons will be completely dispelled;
merit and virtue will blaze forth, and swift accomplishment will be attained.
Furthermore, one should empower scented water by reciting the mantra one thousand and eight times.
If one sprinkles [this water] upon the body, all demonic fevers (yakṣa-jvara) will be eliminated.
Furthermore, another method is to take a single tail-feather of a peacock and empower it one hundred and eight times.
If one brushes [the powder] upon the bodies of those who have been struck by poison, they shall all be cured.
Furthermore, there is another method: take earthworm dung and smear it upon a small circular altar;
sitting upon it, recite the mantra ten thousand times.

First, one should perform the preliminary rites for accomplishment; once the preliminary practitioner has achieved success through the mantras, attaining merit, efficacy, and divine verification, they may thereafter recite the mantra one thousand and eight times daily for seven days, without selecting specific dates or astrological configurations (*nakṣatra*).
One will immediately obtain one thousand gold coins.
Furthermore, by reciting the mantra to empower a cord or a sash,
or by sprinkling water, it becomes a protection for the body.
Reciting it twice establishes the boundary of the cardinal directions;
reciting the mantra three times protects one's companions;
and reciting it four times protects the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight,
one should fast for one day and one night. Then,
take *gomaya* (cow dung) from a mother cow and her calf of the same color that has not yet fallen to the ground.
The preceptor assumes the form of a youth.
He prepares a small altar, places the image upon it,
and extensively arranges offerings upon that altar.
Recite the mantra one hundred thousand times before the image;
when the image moves its head and other signs of efficacy appear,
you should know that whatever matters you contemplate will all be accomplished.
The Vajrakumāra manifests his form within a dream,
instructing one on what actions should be performed and what should not be done.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, one fasts for one day and one night.
Take mustard seeds and clarified butter;
perform one thousand and eight *homa* offerings,
and you will obtain one thousand gold coins as well as ornaments.
Furthermore, there is another method: take śrīveṣṭaka wood and kindle a fire;
perform one hundred thousand *homa* offerings with *guluccha* grass sprouts, and you will immediately obtain one thousand cows.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
for the sake of the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all sentient beings,
spoke this general ritual manual.
This is for the sake of those in the future age of the Dharma’s decline who practice with pure faith and delight in the Mahāyāna,
as well as those who are indolent and lazy, lacking both wisdom and skillful means.
Swiftly gather merit and wisdom to cultivate the true words and deeds,
acting as a sovereign who protects and upholds the True Dharma,
so that the nation’s borders and its people may be blessed with abundance and joy.
To eliminate all calamities and bring forth auspiciousness and merit,
he then spoke this sublime gateway of mantras.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi—
He immediately emitted light from between his eyebrows,
illuminating and empowering [the assembly].
You should receive with the highest reverence what I have spoken.
The ritual procedures for the accomplishment of the Great Fierce Vidyārāja, Vajrakumāra, including the pacification of calamities,
soaring through the air, and so forth— just as in the aforementioned rites, you all must provide assistance and protection;
cause this dharma to be swiftly accomplished, and do not give rise to doubt.
Thus it was practiced according to the Dharma.
The *Āryakrodhavajrakumārabodhisattvasādhanavidhi-sūtra*, Scroll II.
